items.title: Ray Lopez Interview, 1958-08-30
items.q: Henny, Merritt, Richie, Abby and Georgie. And doublehead the uncle. Played bass. And they'd stand on the corner and play stuff, see?

ctx.x: George Brunus, the younger brother. Yeah, little Georgie. Said that Henny was the greatest in the family. That's right.

Now, here's the funny thing. I played the Orphan in 1919, see? And I'm going out in the Irish Channel to see some folks. And who's sitting across the street on the box step with his big bare feet was this punk, Georgie. Yeah. Used to play alto. You know, the old man had a spasm band. Used to play around the markets on Sunday morning. Henny, Merritt, Richie, Abby and Georgie. And doublehead the uncle. Played bass. And they'd stand on the corner and play stuff, see? So, to make a long story short, He said, hey,…
Chicago, yeah. He went up there in about 1921 or so. Yeah.
